Both directives open by describing the Red Cross's work in war, peace, disaster relief, blood programs, and service at home and abroad; designate a named official as Chairman of the Government Unit; request departmental support; call for an adequate internal campaign organization; and direct field offices to cooperate with local Red Cross chapters. C05 uses much the same machinery for the 1953 campaign, while C25 is a weaker parallel involving another federal charitable campaign.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"In peace and war, at home and abroad, the work of the American Red Cross symbolizes American courage and compassion. Through its blood program for civilians and the armed forces ... relief work after flood, fire and hurricane","parent_excerpt":"In war it renders so many services ... to men fighting for freedom ... In peace the American spirit of people helping people is demonstrated ... In disasters it mitigates sufferings caused by fire ... tornado and flood. Through its civilian and military blood donor program","explanation":"The child closely reprises C10's sequence of Red Cross functions, including war and peace service, disaster relief, and civilian and military blood programs."},{"child_excerpt":"I have asked the Honorable Sinclair Weeks, Secretary of Commerce, to act as the Chairman of the Government Unit.","parent_excerpt":"the Honorable Arthur E. Summerfield, the Postmaster General, whom I have designated as Chairman of the Government Unit","explanation":"Both annual campaign memoranda install a Cabinet official as Chairman of the Government Unit using nearly identical language."},{"child_excerpt":"request all officials and employees of your department, in Washington and the field, to cooperate with their respective local chapters and to form an organization adequate to raise the amount desired from your department","parent_excerpt":"create within your department a Red Cross organization adequate to give everyone an opportunity to contribute and attain the goal desired from your department. Likewise ... request all personnel in your departmental field offices to help the Red Cross by generous cooperation with their local Red Cross Chapters.","explanation":"This is a distinctive parallel bundle of operative instructions: create an adequate departmental organization, pursue the department's goal, and have field personnel cooperate with local chapters."}]}
